# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 21 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 21 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_021_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 21

**21:1** When Herod perceived that he had been deceived by the Magi, he was angry and sent his executioners, saying: "Kill all the male children two years old and under."

**21:2** Mary, hearing that the infants were being killed, was afraid and took the infant and wrapped him in swaddling clothes and laid him in a manger.

**21:3** But Elizabeth, hearing that John was being sought, took him and fled into the hill country. And she looked for a place to hide him, and there was none. And Elizabeth groaned and cried out: "O mountain of God, receive a mother with her child!" For Elizabeth was unable to climb further. And immediately the mountain was split open and received her. And the light shone through the mountain to guide her, for an angel of the Lord was with them, protecting them.

---

## Translator's Note

The Massacre of the Innocents (21:1) follows Matthew 2:16 but specifies "male children" explicitly (the Greek text varies by MS — some say "infants," some say "males"). Mary's response is to place Jesus in the manger (21:2) — a detail that implies the cave birth setting of ch. 19 continues. The Elizabeth episode (21:3) is entirely the Protevangelium's own: Elizabeth's miraculous concealment in the mountain has no Gospel parallel and is one of the text's most distinctive legendary contributions. The split mountain becomes an icon of divine protection in early Christian imagination.
